subtype: Approach: sleeping properly the night before and light revision [Thinking]
passage: I'm Yogesh, and the maths exam was on Monday morning. My friend Mohit said he would stay up till midnight, and for a moment I thought I should too. Then I remembered the last late night, when my eyes stung and my mind went blank on the first question. Sleepy me will not remember anything, I thought. So at eight I read only my summary sheet, the short points I had written. Papa put down his newspaper. "Bed already, my boy?" "I'll trust what I know," I said. By half past nine, I was asleep.

qa.q: What time did Yogesh go to sleep?
qa.a: He was asleep by half past nine.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling as he chose to read only the summary sheet and go to bed?
qa.a: He felt confident and calm about trusting what he had learned. He remembered how bad a late night felt and did not want to repeat it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Yogesh use if he still felt worried, and why?
qa.a: He could write down the three things he is least sure about and glance at them once. Then his worry has a small place to go and he can still sleep.

qa.q: How does Mohit's plan look next to Yogesh's?
qa.a: Mohit's plan to stay up till midnight might feel like working harder, but he could be drowsy on the first question, as Yogesh remembered feeling after a late night.

grounding: A boy decides staying up late would only make him drowsy in the exam, so he revises summary points early, sleeps by half past nine and trusts what he learned.
